title: Add batch convert command for directory processing
description: Add 'ingestr convert <dir>' support for batch converting entire directories. Features: 1) Recursive directory traversal with --recursive 2) File extension filtering with --extensions 3) Parallel processing with --parallel N 4) Output directory structure mirroring with --output-dir 5) Dry-run mode with --dry-run 6) Progress reporting 7) Summary statistics at end

title: Add ingestr convert file command
description: Add `ingestr convert <FILE>` for quick ad-hoc conversion to Markdown (with YAML frontmatter). Default outputs to stdout; `--output PATH` writes to file; respects `--json/--yaml` and `--dry-run`. Includes unit test for frontmatter+content rendering.

title: Add VLM processor for image understanding
description: Add optional VLM processing for images using EAVS as the LLM backend. Design: 1) Talk to EAVS at localhost:3000 using OpenAI format 2) Use X-Provider header to select backend (ollama, openai, anthropic) 3) Configurable prompts per file type 4) Config section [processors.vlm] with enabled, eavs_url, provider, model, prompts 5) CLI flags --vlm and --vlm-prompt for ad-hoc 6) NO direct LLM code in ingestr - just HTTP to EAVS

title: Add stdin support for convert command
description: Add stdin support to convert command for piping content. Usage: cat file.html | ingestr convert --from html. Features: 1) --from flag to specify input format 2) Auto-detect format from content when possible 3) Support common formats: html, pdf (base64), docx (base64), plain text 4) Output to stdout by default for further piping

title: Add OCR processor backend for scanned documents
description: Add optional OCR processing for scanned PDFs and images. Design: 1) Configurable backend (tesseract, surya, easyocr) 2) Language configuration 3) Fallback chain: try markitdown first, OCR if no text extracted 4) Config section [processors.ocr] with enabled, backend, languages fields 5) CLI flag --ocr to enable ad-hoc

title: Add processor pipeline configuration
description: Add configurable processor pipeline that determines how files are processed. Design: 1) [processors.pipeline] config section 2) Define order of processors to try 3) File type routing (e.g., images -> VLM, PDFs -> markitdown then OCR fallback) 4) Processor chaining (e.g., OCR output fed to VLM for summarization) 5) Default pipeline: markitdown only. Example config: pipeline = ['markitdown', 'ocr_fallback', 'vlm_images']

title: Add 'ingestr convert' ad-hoc command for single file conversion
description: Add a new 'ingestr convert <file>' command that converts a single file to markdown and outputs to stdout (or optional --output file). Uses markitdown by default. Should support: 1) Output to stdout for piping 2) Optional --output <path> for file output 3) Optional --json for structured output with frontmatter as JSON 4) Same frontmatter format as service mode for consistency

title: Structure extraction: --toc flag
description: Extract document structure (headings, page count, tables) without full content. Show heading hierarchy with estimated token counts per section. Enables agents to scan structure first, then request specific sections.

title: Add GitHub release workflow for ingestr binaries (linux amd64+arm64)
Native URL support
description: If input looks like a URL, fetch and convert in one step. Handles HTML pages and PDF links. Follows redirects. Combines with all other flags (--max-tokens, --toc, etc).

title: Section-level retrieval: --section flag
description: Return only a specific section by heading number or name. Works with --toc output. E.g. --section '2.1' returns only that subsection. Dramatically reduces token usage for large documents.

title: Make convert the default subcommand
description: If the first argument is a file path or URL, assume convert. No need to type 'ingestr convert file.pdf' when 'ingestr file.pdf' is unambiguous. Every other subcommand is a known keyword.

title: Page-level access: --pages flag
description: For PDFs: convert specific pages only. --pages 1-3,7 converts only those pages. Agents often know which page they need from a prior TOC scan.

title: Clipboard support: --clipboard flag
description: Read from system clipboard. Handles text, HTML, and images (via VLM). Detects content type automatically.

title: Conform ingestr to byteowlz template standards (phase 0)
Strip frontmatter by default, add --meta flag
description: Default output should be pure markdown with no YAML frontmatter. Add --meta flag to include metadata when explicitly requested. When --json is used, metadata goes in JSON fields, not embedded in markdown string.

title: Table-aware conversion
description: Detect tables in source and ensure they survive as proper markdown tables. For XLSX, use sheet name as heading. For --json output, include a structured tables array with headers and rows.

title: Post-processing cleaning pipeline
description: After markitdown converts, run a cleaning pass: collapse excessive whitespace, strip repeated headers/footers (detected by repetition across pages), remove page numbers, fix broken line wraps from PDF column layouts. On by default with --raw to skip.

title: Token budget control: --max-tokens / --max-chars
description: Truncate output to a token/character budget. Intelligent truncation at section boundaries, not mid-sentence. Append truncation notice with remaining token count so agent can request next chunk. Support --offset for pagination.

title: Conversion cache
description: Cache converted output keyed by file hash + conversion options. Second conversion is instant. Cache lives in XDG_CACHE_HOME/ingestr/. --no-cache to bypass. Add cache clear and cache stats subcommands.

title: [feature] Optional PPTX → sldr ingestion path (emit a sldr slide library, not one markdown blob)
description:
## Goal

A modular, opt-in output target so `ingestr convert deck.pptx --to sldr` produces files sldr can use directly: one markdown slide per PPTX slide, media as siblings, notes preserved. Today PPTX converts to a single markdown document (markitdown), which loses the slide boundary that sldr's library model depends on.

Why here and not in sldr: sldr's ADR-0004 (as amended by its ADR-0010/0011) says the sldr core never contains an importer for arbitrary PPTX; importing foreign decks is a plain-file-producing step outside the binary. ingestr is exactly that step. sldr's own `sldr-pptx` crate only round-trips decks sldr generated.

## Output shape (the sldr "ingest target")

```
<out>/
  slides/<deck-slug>/
    01-<slide-slug>.md
    02-<slide-slug>.md
    media/<deck-slug>-<n>-<m>.png|jpg|svg
  playlists/<deck-slug>.toml        # ordered list of the slides above, no flavor
  ingest-manifest.json               # provenance: source path+hash, per-slide mapping, dispositions
```

Each slide `.md` = YAML frontmatter + markdown body, matching sldr's slide format:

```
---
title: <slide title placeholder text, or first text line>
subtitle: <subtitle placeholder if present>
source: <deck file name>            # attribution
tags: [imported, pptx]
layout: default                     # NEVER guessed — always default; agent/studio picks later
---
<body text and bullets as markdown; bullet nesting preserved>

![alt](media/<deck-slug>-<n>-<m>.png)

::notes::
<speaker notes, verbatim>
```

Rules:
- One markdown file per PPTX slide, numbered to keep deck order; playlist carries the order.
- Title/subtitle placeholders → frontmatter `title` / `subtitle`; other text boxes → body in reading order (top-left to bottom-right).
- Bullets → markdown lists with nesting; tables → markdown tables; everything else → plain paragraphs.
- Pictures extracted to `media/` and referenced relatively; SmartArt/charts/groups: rasterize if a renderer is available, else emit a `<!-- ingestr: unsupported <kind> on slide n -->` comment and record it in the manifest. Never drop silently.
- Notes slide → `::notes::` section (sldr's speaker-notes marker).
- No layout inference, no flavor extraction, no per-slide geometry. Layout is `default`; theme colors/fonts may be *reported* in the manifest for an agent to build a flavor from, but nothing is written to sldr's flavor format.
- `--to sldr` is a separate processor/output module so the default markitdown path stays untouched.

## Manifest

`ingest-manifest.json`: `{ source: {path, sha256, slide_count}, slides: [{index, file, title, unsupported: [...]}], theme: {colors, fonts} }`. Purely informational; sldr does not read it, agents do.

## Acceptance

- Synthetic fixture deck (title slide, bullets with nesting, picture, notes, one SmartArt) converts; `sldr build <deck-slug>` in a library pointed at `<out>` renders every slide.
- Manifest lists the SmartArt as unsupported; no text from the fixture is missing from the output.
- Plain `ingestr convert deck.pptx` output is unchanged.

## Related

- sldr: docs/adr/0011-zone-document-is-the-editor-and-pptx-model.md, trx-3f4w (studio epic). The studio's new-slide/finder flows are how imported slides get layouts and flavors afterwards.
